plan.objective: What the benchmark as a whole measures.
plan.planner_notes: Optional decisions that apply across the plan.

dimensions.name: Dimension name
dimensions.measurement_target: The capability or behavior measured independently by this dimension.
dimensions.boundary: What this dimension includes and how it differs from adjacent dimensions.
dimensions.approach: How tasks in this dimension should elicit and measure the target capability.
content_requirements: Content that this dimension must cover.
exclusions: Content or confounds that this dimension must avoid.

content_design.purpose: What the covered task or tasks measure within the dimension.
content_design.description: A concrete concept for one complex task, or a shared content description for multiple simpler tasks.
coverage_requirements: Required content coverage within these tasks.
variation_requirements: How multiple tasks using this description must differ.
task_relationships: Optional relationships or dependencies among the covered tasks.
exclusions: Content, shortcuts, or confounds these tasks must avoid.

input_requirements.description: What information or materials the covered tasks receive.
input_requirements.format_or_schema: Required input format, structure, or schema.
shared_inputs: Inputs shared by the covered tasks.
input_requirements.per_task_variation: How inputs should vary among concrete tasks.

asset_requirements.role: Why the asset is needed by the task.

interaction_requirements.mode: single_turn, multi_turn, tool_use, environment_interaction, or mixed
interaction_requirements.followup_mode: For multi_turn only: adaptive or scripted.
interaction_requirements.statefulness: What state persists and how it may change.
interaction_requirements.turn_or_step_policy: Expected turn structure, step policy, or interaction horizon.
allowed_action_or_tool_categories: Capabilities the evaluated subject may use.
interaction_requirements.observation_model: What feedback or observations actions should produce.
interaction_requirements.completion_condition: How the interaction reaches a successful or terminal state.
trajectory_requirements: Required, forbidden, or score-relevant process behavior.

environment_requirements.category: dialogue, workspace, code_sandbox, docker_workspace, or gui_desktop
environment_requirements.purpose: Why an execution environment is necessary.
environment_requirements.initial_state: The high-level state in which each task must begin.
required_software_or_services: Software or services needed to make the task possible.
environment_requirements.network_requirements: Whether and why network access is needed.
constraints: Environment properties the Builder must preserve or avoid.

output_requirements.description: What a successful response or completed task should produce.
output_requirements.format_or_schema: Required output format, schema, or interface.
required_components: Required parts of the response or result.

artifacts.kind: file, dataset, report, media, repository change, or another deliverable
artifacts.description: What the artifact must contain or accomplish.

constraints: Output properties, limits, or forbidden shortcuts.

components.method: exact answer, rubric, executable test, artifact inspection, final-state check, trajectory check, comparison, or another method
components.oracle_type: The kind of reference, evaluator, invariant, or expected state used as the oracle.
criteria: The substantive criteria that determine correctness or quality.
components.partial_credit: Whether partial credit is allowed and what it should represent.
components.verification_direction: How the Builder should make scoring deterministic or reproducible.

scoring_contract.aggregation: How multiple checks, turns, artifacts, trials, or sub-scores combine.
scoring_contract.trial_policy: Optional repetition, sampling, or stochastic-evaluation requirements.
failure_conditions: Conditions that must result in task failure.

source_plan.strategy: self_contained, generated, source_backed, imported_dataset, or mixed
search_queries: Queries the Builder may use to find suitable material.
requirements: Authority, recency, reproducibility, licensing, or provenance requirements.
usage_guidance: How sources should inform tasks without being copied mechanically.

construction_requirements: Requirements for turning this description into the requested number of complete tasks.

type_specific_requirements.protocol: Optional namespaced protocol or task-type extension identifier.

requirements.extension_field: Only requirements that cannot be expressed by the universal fields above.

blueprints.title: Blueprint title
blueprints.grouping_rationale: Why these task designs naturally belong in one Builder job.
blueprints.workload_reason: Why one Task Builder call can implement all referenced tasks at sufficient quality.
